newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan can achieve 1.9 pct growth in 1997/98 -- EPA.
newsitem.headline: Japan can achieve 1.9 pct growth in 1997/98 -- EPA.

text.p: Japan can achieve its target of 1.9 percent growth in gross domestic product (GDP) in fiscal 1997/98, Economic Planning Agency (EPA) Vice Minister Shimpei Nukaya told reporters on Friday.
"Even if there were a considerable deceleration in the April to June period, we can achieve the government's target of around 1.9 percent centring on domestic demand," he said.
Nukaya said a dip in private consumption after the rise in the consumption tax from three percent to five percent on April 1 would generally be absorbed in the April to June period.
Corporate capital spending was generally steady while government spending had fallen up until March, but the decline was likely to halt, he said.
"There are not many factors to hinder growth," he said.
He added that external demand was unlikely to grow drastically but it was also unlikely to make a negative contribution to economic growth.

Asked about the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development's (OECD) economic outlook for Japan, Nukaya said its estimates for calendar 1997 did not differ so much from those of the Japanese government.
The Paris-based OECD said in a twice-yearly report on Friday that Japan's GDP growth would slow to 2.3 percent in 1997. It forecast GDP growth would rise to 2.9 percent in 1998.
Nukaya said that in the January to March data, the growth came to a considerable extent from a rush in demand ahead of the consumption tax increase.
Private consumption was generally strong during this period while government public spending fell, he said.

He said self-sustainable economic growth centring on private demand was appearing but the government needed to watch economic conditions for the coming month to confirm that the shift in demand from government to private sector had been completed.
